c: She's hanging a picture on the wall.
qs.e: La femme tape sur le clavier d'un ordinateur portable. Le mug, le cadre et la lampe sont bien visibles, mais aucune de ces actions n'a lieu : c'est le piège classique « objet présent, action inexacte ».

c: Boxes are being loaded onto a truck.
A cart is being pushed down an aisle.
Some boxes have been stacked on a cart.
qs.e: Personne n'apparaît sur la photo : une forme « is/are being + participe » (action en cours, donc faite par quelqu'un) est impossible. « Have been stacked » décrit un état visible. Les étagères contiennent des cartons, donc (D) est faux.

c: Chairs have been arranged around a table.
Some people are attending a meeting.
A screen is being installed on the wall.
Some chairs are stacked in a corner.
qs.e: La salle est vide et les chaises entourent la table. (B) mentionne des personnes absentes ; (C) utilise « being installed » sans personne ; les chaises ne sont pas empilées.

c: A man is folding up a ladder.
A man is painting a wall.
A ladder is leaning against a tree.
A man is standing on a ladder.
qs.e: L'homme est debout sur un escabeau et lève le bras vers le plafonnier. Il ne plie pas l'échelle, ne peint pas, et il n'y a pas d'arbre : la scène est en intérieur.

c: A woman is riding a bicycle.
Some bicycles are parked in a row.
qs.e: Des vélos sont garés côte à côte dans un râtelier. Personne ne roule ni ne répare : « being repaired » et « being planted » supposent une action en cours.

c: They're seated across from each other.
The woman is opening a door.
qs.e: Les deux personnes se serrent la main, debout. La porte est fermée et personne n'échange de cartes : attention aux contextes « bureau » qui rendent les autres options plausibles.

c: A server is pouring water into a glass.
A customer is paying the bill.
Some plates are being cleared from a table.
qs.e: Le serveur verse de l'eau dans un verre. Les assiettes sont encore sur la table : « being cleared » est faux. Personne ne paie l'addition.

c: A boat is passing under a bridge.
People are fishing from a pier.
Some boats are docked at a pier.
qs.e: Les bateaux sont amarrés le long d'un ponton. Il n'y a ni pont, ni personnes : ici encore, « being painted » est impossible sans personne.

c: She's planting flowers in a garden.
qs.e: La femme arrose des plantes en pot avec un arrosoir. La fenêtre reste fermée et la scène se passe à l'intérieur, pas dans un jardin.

c: He's stacking books on a table.
He's reaching for a book on a shelf.
qs.e: L'homme tend le bras vers un livre placé en hauteur dans la bibliothèque. La table est vide (pas de livres empilés) et il ne lit pas.

c: A man is adjusting a microphone.
A woman is pointing at a chart.
qs.e: Une femme montre un graphique projeté. Le public est assis mais n'applaudit pas ; aucun micro n'est visible. Méfiez-vous de « chart » répété dans un faux énoncé (C).

c: Some people are waiting at a bus stop.
Passengers are getting off a train.
A bus is parked inside a garage.
qs.e: Trois personnes attendent sous l'abribus. Il n'y a pas de train ; le bus est dans la rue, pas dans un garage ; personne ne traverse.

c: Coffee is being poured into some cups.
A coffee machine is being repaired.
Some cups have been placed beside a coffee machine.
Some cups are hanging from hooks.
qs.e: Aucune personne : seules les formes d'état (« have been placed ») conviennent. Les tasses sont posées sur le comptoir, pas suspendues.

c: A worker is pushing a wheelbarrow.
A worker is removing his helmet.
A wheelbarrow is being lifted onto a truck.
qs.e: L'ouvrier, casque sur la tête, pousse une brouette chargée de briques. Il ne retire pas son casque et aucun camion n'apparaît.

qs.q: Where should I put these boxes?
qs.e: « Where » attend un lieu. (A) répond par « yes » à une question ouverte — toujours faux avec une question en WH ; (C) donne une quantité.

qs.q: When does the training session start?
qs.e: « When » = moment. (B) répondrait à « Where » ; (C) parle au passé d'une session qui n'a pas commencé.

qs.q: Who's in charge of the new project?
qs.e: « Who » attend une personne. (B) répète « charge » avec un autre sens (des frais) : piège sonore typique.

qs.q: Why was the meeting postponed?
c: The director is out of town.
qs.e: « Why » attend une raison : l'absence du directeur. (B) recycle « meet », un mot de la même famille que « meeting ».

qs.q: Would you like me to print the agenda?
qs.e: « Would you like me to… ? » est une offre : on accepte ou on refuse poliment. (A) et (C) reprennent « like » et « print » sans répondre.

qs.q: How much does the software upgrade cost?
qs.e: « How much » + cost = un prix. « About two hours » répondrait à « How long ».

qs.q: Didn't you send the invoice yesterday?
c: No, I'm doing it this morning.
qs.e: Une question négative se traite comme une question oui/non normale : « No, I'm doing it this morning » est cohérent. (C) commence par « yes » mais la suite n'a aucun sens.

qs.q: Should we take a taxi or the train to the airport?
c: The train is faster at this hour.
qs.e: Question à choix (A or B) : « yes/no » est presque toujours faux. La bonne réponse choisit une option et justifie.

qs.q: The client called while you were out.
qs.e: Face à une affirmation, la réponse naturelle est souvent une question de suivi. (B) et (C) recyclent « call » et « out ».

qs.q: Can you help me move this desk?
c: Sure, where do you want it?
qs.e: Demande d'aide → acceptation + question pratique. (B) joue sur « move » au sens de « déménager ».

qs.q: Which supplier did you choose?
qs.e: « Which » appelle une sélection : « The one in… ». (C) est un piège de mot dérivé (supplier → supplies).

qs.q: Isn't the report due today?
qs.e: Réponse indirecte typique : on ne dit pas « no » mais on donne l'information qui y répond (le délai a été prolongé).

qs.q: How long will the renovations take?
qs.e: « How long » demande une durée. (A) piège sur « long » employé comme adjectif de taille.

qs.q: Who should I send the signed contract to?
c: Mr. Patel in the legal department.
qs.e: « Who » = une personne. (C) répondrait à « How should I send it? ».

qs.q: What time does the store close on Saturdays?
qs.e: « What time » = une heure. (A) joue sur « close » (fermer) / « close to » (près de), qui se prononcent différemment.

qs.q: Have you finished reviewing the budget proposal?
c: A proposal for the new office.
I'm still on the second page.
qs.e: Réponse indirecte : « Je suis encore à la page 2 » signifie « non, pas encore ». Les deux autres réutilisent « budget » et « proposal ».

qs.q: Why don't we have lunch on the terrace today?
c: The terrace is on the roof.
qs.e: « Why don't we… ? » n'est pas une question en « why » mais une suggestion : on l'accepte ou on la refuse.

qs.q: Is the new printer working yet?
c: Yes, the technician fixed it this morning.
He's working on the third floor.
qs.e: Question fermée → « Yes » + justification. (B) recycle « working » avec un autre sujet (he).

qs.q: Where can I find the quarterly sales figures?
qs.e: « Where » = un emplacement (le lecteur partagé). (B) joue sur le sens de « quarterly » (trimestriel).

qs.q: You're going to the conference in Berlin, aren't you?
c: No, I'll be on vacation that week.
qs.e: Question-tag (« aren't you? ») = demande de confirmation. (C) est un piège sonore Berlin/Brazil.

qs.q: Could you send me a copy of the schedule?
c: I'll e-mail it to you right away.
qs.e: Demande polie → acceptation. « coffee » / « copy » et « schedule » / « scheduled » sont des pièges sonores.

qs.q: When will the new manager start?
qs.e: « Not until next month » (pas avant le mois prochain) est une réponse de temps fréquente au TOEIC.

qs.q: Do you want to review the slides now or after lunch?
c: Let's do it now, while we have time.
qs.e: Question à choix : on choisit (now). (A) commence par « yes » et utilise le mauvais temps (reviewed).

qs.q: The elevator is out of order again.
qs.e: Réaction logique au problème annoncé. (B) piège sur « order » (commander).

qs.q: How did the client presentation go?
qs.e: « How did … go? » demande comment ça s'est passé. (A) reprend « go » au sens de « se déplacer ».

qs.q: Who's going to replace Mr. Kim while he's away?
c: He'll be away for two weeks.
qs.e: « It hasn't been decided yet » / « I'm not sure » sont souvent les bonnes réponses dans le format actuel. (C) : piège replace/place.

qs.q: Should I book a table for four or six?
c: The table is in the corner.
Make it six, just in case.
qs.e: On choisit une option (six). (C) répond « yes » à une question à choix.

qs.q: Why is the parking lot so crowded today?
c: There's a job fair in the building.
qs.e: Une raison est attendue : un salon de l'emploi attire du monde. (C) répète « crowded » sans expliquer.

qs.q: Would you mind closing the window?
qs.e: « Would you mind… ? » signifie « Cela vous dérange-t-il… ? » : « Not at all » = « pas du tout, je le fais ».

qs.q: What did you think of the new logo?
c: I think it's on the Web site.
It's simple and easy to recognize.
qs.e: On demande une opinion → une appréciation. (A) recycle « think » sans donner d'avis.

qs.q: Is this seat taken?
qs.e: « Is this seat taken? » = « Cette place est-elle prise ? ». « No, go ahead » invite à s'asseoir. (B) et (C) répètent « take ».

qs.q: Our sales figures are lower than expected this quarter.
c: The figures are on page four.
Let's discuss it at Monday's meeting.
qs.e: Réponse constructive à une mauvaise nouvelle. (B) recycle « expect » ; (A) répète « figures ».

qs.q: How often is the equipment inspected?
qs.e: « How often » = fréquence. (A) répondrait à « By whom? ».

qs.q: Aren't you supposed to be in Lyon today?
qs.e: Réponse indirecte : le voyage a été annulé, donc il n'est pas à Lyon. (C) joue sur « supposed / suppose ».

qs.q: Where's the nearest post office?
c: I posted it on the board.
qs.e: « Where » → un lieu. (A) : piège « post office » / « posted ».

qs.q: Can I pay by credit card?
c: The price is on the tag.
qs.e: Réponse négative polie et précise. (A) recycle « card » dans un autre sens.

qs.q: Let's ask Maria to lead the workshop.
qs.e: On approuve la suggestion. (B) piège workshop/shop ; (C) piège ask/asked.

qs.q: Which floor is the accounting department on?
qs.e: « Which floor » → un étage. (A) : « accounting » / « count ».

qs.q: Has the shipment from Tokyo arrived?
c: Let me check with the warehouse.
qs.e: « Let me check… » est une réponse indirecte très fréquente et toujours logique. (A) : shipment/ship.

qs.q: Why don't you take tomorrow off?
c: Thanks, but I have a deadline.
qs.e: « Why don't you… ? » est une suggestion. Répondre « Because… » est le piège classique. (C) : piège sur « off ».

title: Conversation — commande en retard
script: Hi, I'm calling about the printer we ordered from your Web site last week. It was supposed to arrive on Monday, but we still haven't received it.
I'm sorry about that. Let me check your order... It looks like the shipment was delayed because of a problem at our distribution center. It should reach you tomorrow morning.
Tomorrow's fine, but we really need it before our training session on Thursday.
It will definitely be there. And to make up for the delay, I'll take fifteen percent off your invoice.

qs.q: Why is the woman calling?
qs.e: « we still haven't received it » → la commande n'est pas arrivée. L'idée principale se trouve presque toujours dans les deux premières répliques.

qs.q: According to the man, what caused the delay?
c: A problem at a distribution center
qs.e: « delayed because of a problem at our distribution center » — reprise quasi littérale.

qs.q: What does the man offer to do?
qs.e: « take fifteen percent off your invoice » = baisser le prix. La bonne réponse est presque toujours une paraphrase.

title: Conversation à trois — salon professionnel
script: Sophie, Daniel, have you two had a chance to look at the budget for the trade fair in Frankfurt?
I have, and I'm a bit concerned. The cost of renting a booth has gone up almost thirty percent since last year.
That's a lot. What if we shared a booth with our partners from Rotterdam? They mentioned they were planning to attend too.
That could work. I'll e-mail them this afternoon to see if they're interested.
Good. And Daniel, could you find out whether the organizers offer an early-registration discount?

qs.q: What are the speakers mainly discussing?
qs.e: Le sujet est posé dès la 1re réplique : « the budget for the trade fair ».

qs.q: What does the woman say about the booth?
c: It is far from the entrance.
qs.e: « has gone up almost thirty percent » = une hausse de prix.

qs.q: What is Daniel asked to do?
qs.e: Daniel doit vérifier s'il existe une réduction pour inscription anticipée. Piège : c'est la femme, pas Daniel, qui contactera les partenaires.

title: Conversation — installation de logiciel
script: Kevin, the new accounting software is supposed to be installed on everyone's computer by Friday. How's it going?
Well, I've finished the second floor, but the third floor is going to take longer. Several of the computers there are too old to run the program.
Hmm. We might have to order new machines, then. Do you know how many we'd need?
About twelve. I'll put together a list with the models and prices so you can show it to the finance director.
Thanks. But remember, the budget meeting is tomorrow morning.

qs.q: What is the man doing this week?
qs.e: Il installe le nouveau logiciel de comptabilité, étage par étage.

qs.q: What problem does the man mention?
qs.e: « too old to run the program » = des ordinateurs obsolètes (outdated).

qs.q: What does the man mean when he says, "I'm on it"?
c: He is standing on a platform.
He will start the task immediately.
He has already attended the meeting.
qs.e: « I'm on it » = « je m'en occupe tout de suite ». Les questions d'intention testent le sens en contexte, pas le sens littéral.

title: Conversation + graphique — accueil
script: Excuse me, I have an interview with Ms. Alvarez at ten o'clock. I was told her office is on the second floor.
Ms. Alvarez? She used to be in Human Resources, but she moved to the marketing team last month. You'll find her one floor up from there.
Oh, thank you. Do I need a visitor's pass?
Yes. Please sign in here and show me a photo ID, and I'll print one for you.

qs.q: Why is the man visiting the building?
qs.e: « I have an interview with Ms. Alvarez ».

qs.q: Look at the graphic. Which floor will the man go to?
qs.e: Ms. Alvarez a rejoint le marketing, « one floor up » par rapport aux RH (étage 2) → étage 3. Les questions à graphique exigent de croiser l'audio et le document.

qs.q: What does the woman ask the man to do?
qs.e: « show me a photo ID » = présenter une pièce d'identité.

title: Conversation — réservation au restaurant
script: Hello, I'd like to reserve a table for eight people this Friday at seven thirty. It's for a colleague's retirement dinner.
Let me see... Friday's usually our busiest night. I'm afraid we only have tables for up to six at seven thirty.
Oh, that's a shame. Is there anything later in the evening?
We could seat eight at nine o'clock in our private room upstairs. It's quieter, too.
Nine is a bit late, but... you know what, the private room sounds perfect. Let's do that.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the dinner?
qs.e: « a colleague's retirement dinner » = un départ à la retraite.

qs.q: Why does the woman say, "Friday's usually our busiest night"?
c: To explain why a request may be difficult
To ask the man to arrive early
qs.e: Elle prépare l'annonce d'une mauvaise nouvelle : pas de table pour huit à 19 h 30.

qs.q: What does the man decide to do?
qs.e: « the private room sounds perfect. Let's do that. »

title: Conversation + graphique — départs de trains
script: Mark, our meeting with the client in Brussels starts at noon. Which train were you planning to take?
The nine-oh-five. But I just checked the board, and it's running forty minutes late.
Then we should take the next one. It gets us there with plenty of time to spare, and we can go over the presentation on the way.
Good idea. I'll change our tickets at the counter—you grab us some coffee.

qs.q: Why are the speakers traveling to Brussels?
qs.e: « our meeting with the client in Brussels ».

qs.q: Look at the graphic. Which platform will the speakers most likely go to?
qs.e: Le train suivant celui de 9 h 05 est celui de 9 h 45, voie 6.

qs.q: What will the man do next?
qs.e: « I'll change our tickets at the counter ». Piège : c'est la femme qui ira chercher le café.

title: Conversation à trois — entretien d'embauche
script: Thanks for joining us, Ms. Okoro. As I mentioned on the phone, Tom and I will be conducting the interview together.
Thank you for having me. I'm really excited about this position.
We were impressed by your experience managing social media campaigns. Could you tell us about one that was especially successful?
Sure. Last year I led a campaign for a sportswear brand that doubled their online sales in three months.
That's impressive. Before we continue, would you mind if we recorded the interview? Our director is traveling and would like to listen to it later.

qs.q: Who most likely is Ms. Okoro?
qs.e: On lui fait passer un entretien pour un poste : c'est une candidate.

qs.q: What does Ms. Okoro say she did last year?
c: She moved to a new city.
qs.e: « I led a campaign … that doubled their online sales ».

qs.q: Why does the man ask for permission?
qs.e: « would you mind if we recorded the interview? »

title: Conversation — déménagement de bureaux
script: Hi Rachel, the moving company just called. They can't come on Saturday as planned. Their truck needs repairs.
Oh no. We've already told everyone to pack their desks by Friday afternoon. Did they suggest another date?
They offered Sunday morning, but they'd charge an extra two hundred dollars for weekend overtime.
Hmm, that's still cheaper than closing the office on a weekday. Go ahead and confirm Sunday, and I'll let the staff know.

qs.q: What are the speakers preparing for?
qs.e: Déménageurs, cartons, bureaux à vider : il s'agit d'un déménagement (relocation).

qs.q: Why did the moving company change its plans?
c: A vehicle needs to be fixed.
qs.e: « Their truck needs repairs » → un véhicule doit être réparé.

qs.q: What does the woman ask the man to do?
qs.e: « Go ahead and confirm Sunday ».

title: Conversation + graphique — traiteur
script: Hello, I'm organizing a lunch for our board meeting next Wednesday, and I'm looking at the catering packages on your Web site.
Great. How many people will be attending?
Twenty. We'd like a hot meal, and dessert is a must—our chairman always asks for it. But we can't go over twenty-five dollars a person.
Then this package is the one for you. I'll e-mail you a menu so you can choose the dishes.

qs.q: What event is the woman organizing?
qs.e: « a lunch for our board meeting ».

qs.q: Look at the graphic. Which package will the woman most likely choose?
qs.e: Repas chaud + dessert + 25 $ maximum → seul « Premium » (24 $) remplit les trois conditions.

qs.q: What will the man send the woman?
qs.e: « I'll e-mail you a menu ».

title: Conversation — service client
script: Customer support, this is Ana speaking. How can I help you?
Hi, I signed up for your photo-editing software last week, but I was charged twice on my credit card.
I'm sorry about that. Could you give me the e-mail address on your account?
Sure, it's j-lee at corvus design dot com.
Thank you... Yes, I see the duplicate charge. I'll process a refund now—it should appear on your statement within five business days.
Five days? Well, I suppose that'll have to do.

qs.q: Why is the man calling?
c: He wants to cancel an order.
qs.e: « I was charged twice on my credit card ».

qs.q: What information does the woman request?
qs.e: « Could you give me the e-mail address on your account? »

qs.q: What does the man imply when he says, "Well, I suppose that'll have to do"?
c: He is pleased with the service.
He accepts a solution he is not happy with.
qs.e: Le ton résigné (« il faudra bien s'en contenter ») montre qu'il accepte sans être satisfait du délai.

title: Conversation — préparation d'une conférence
script: Linda, have you sent out the invitations for the regional sales conference yet?
Not yet. I was waiting for the hotel to confirm the room rate. They just called—it's a hundred and twenty euros a night, including breakfast.
That's within our budget. What about the guest speaker?
Dr. Haddad has agreed to give the keynote address, but she can only stay for the first day.
That's fine. The conference starts on Monday, so let's put her on the schedule for Monday morning.

qs.q: Why have the invitations not been sent yet?
c: The woman was waiting for a price confirmation.
qs.e: « I was waiting for the hotel to confirm the room rate ».

qs.q: What is included in the room rate?
qs.e: « a hundred and twenty euros a night, including breakfast ».

qs.q: When will Dr. Haddad speak?
qs.e: Elle ne reste que le premier jour → lundi matin.

title: Conversation — retour d'un produit
script: Excuse me, I bought this coffee maker here last week, but it stopped working after two days.
I'm sorry to hear that. Do you have your receipt?
Yes, here it is. I'd like to exchange it for the same model, if possible.
Unfortunately, we're out of that model at the moment. We're expecting a delivery on Thursday, though. Or I can give you a full refund right now.
I'll wait for the delivery. Could you call me when it arrives?

qs.q: Where does the conversation most likely take place?
qs.e: Elle rapporte une cafetière achetée dans ce magasin : un magasin d'électroménager. Piège : « café » reprend « coffee ».

qs.q: What problem does the woman mention?
qs.e: « it stopped working after two days » = produit défectueux.

qs.q: What does the woman ask the man to do?
c: Call her when an item arrives
qs.e: « Could you call me when it arrives? » Elle refuse le remboursement.

title: Conversation à trois — refonte d'un site
script: Okay, the client wants the redesigned Web site ready by the end of the month. Raj, where are you with the layouts?
The home page is done, but the product pages still need work. I could use some help with the images.
I can take care of that. I've finished the logo files, so I have some free time this week.
Perfect. Let's meet again on Wednesday to review everything before we send it to the client.

qs.q: What project are the speakers working on?
qs.e: « the redesigned Web site ».

qs.q: What does Raj say he needs help with?
qs.e: « I could use some help with the images ».

qs.q: What will the speakers do on Wednesday?
qs.e: « Let's meet again on Wednesday to review everything ».

title: Annonce — aéroport
script: Good morning, passengers. This is an announcement for travelers on Flight 418 to Montreal. Due to a technical inspection, departure has been delayed by approximately forty-five minutes. The new boarding time is ten fifteen, and boarding will now take place at Gate 22 instead of Gate 18. Passengers with connecting flights in Montreal should speak with an agent at the service desk near Gate 20. We apologize for the inconvenience and thank you for your patience.

qs.q: Where is the announcement being made?
qs.e: Indices : « passengers », « flight 418 », « boarding », « gate ».

qs.q: What has changed?
qs.e: « at Gate 22 instead of Gate 18 ».

qs.q: What are some listeners asked to do?
qs.e: Les passagers en correspondance doivent s'adresser au comptoir de service près de la porte 20.

title: Message téléphonique — imprimerie
script: Hello, this message is for Mr. Bernard. This is Karen from Westside Print Shop. I'm calling to let you know that your order of business cards is ready for pickup. Please note that we've moved to a new location at forty-five Harbor Street, just across from the post office. We're open until seven p.m. on weekdays. If you'd prefer to have the cards delivered, we can do that for a fee of eight euros. Just give us a call back at five five five, zero one four two.

qs.q: Why is the speaker calling?
c: To say that an order is ready
qs.e: « your order of business cards is ready for pickup ».

qs.q: What does the speaker say about the shop?
qs.e: « we've moved to a new location » = relocated (paraphrase).

qs.q: What does the speaker mention about delivery?
qs.e: « for a fee of eight euros ».

title: Bulletin radio — circulation
script: Good afternoon, this is Mike Torres with your five o'clock traffic update. If you're heading downtown, expect delays on Highway 9. A truck has broken down in the left lane near the river bridge, and crews are working to remove it. Traffic is moving very slowly in both directions. If you can, use Elm Avenue instead—it's a few minutes longer, but trust me, you'll get there sooner. And for those of you going to tonight's concert at City Stadium, remember that the parking lots open at six. We'll have the weather forecast right after this short break.

qs.q: What is causing the delay on Highway 9?
qs.e: « A truck has broken down in the left lane ».

qs.q: Why does the speaker say, "trust me, you'll get there sooner"?
qs.e: Il insiste pour convaincre les auditeurs de passer par Elm Avenue.

qs.q: What will listeners most likely hear after the break?
qs.e: « We'll have the weather forecast right after this short break ».

title: Publicité — mobilier de bureau
script: Is your home office ready for the new year? This weekend only, Harmon Furniture is offering thirty percent off all desks and office chairs. Our ergonomic chairs, designed with the help of physical therapists, are perfect for long working days. And if you spend more than five hundred dollars, we'll deliver and assemble your furniture for free. Visit our store on Fulton Road, or shop online at harmon furniture dot com. The sale ends Sunday at six p.m.

qs.q: What is being advertised?
qs.e: Remise de 30 % sur les bureaux et chaises : une promotion de meubles.

qs.q: What is said about the chairs?
c: They were designed with expert help.
qs.e: « designed with the help of physical therapists » → avec l'aide d'experts (kinésithérapeutes).

qs.q: How can customers get free delivery?
c: By spending over a certain amount
qs.e: « if you spend more than five hundred dollars ».

title: Visite guidée + graphique — chocolaterie
script: Welcome to the Linden Chocolate factory, everyone. My name is Paolo, and I'll be your guide this morning. Before we begin, please note that photography is not allowed inside the production areas. We'll start with a short welcome video, and then we'll walk over to see our assembly line. Unfortunately, the quality control lab is closed today for cleaning, so after the assembly line we'll go straight to our tasting area, where you can try our newest flavors. Oh, and don't forget to pick up a free hairnet before entering the factory floor.

qs.q: Who most likely is the speaker?
qs.e: « I'll be your guide this morning ».

qs.q: What are listeners asked not to do?
qs.e: « photography is not allowed inside the production areas ».

qs.q: Look at the graphic. Where will the listeners go after Building 2?
qs.e: Le laboratoire (bâtiment 3) est fermé : après la chaîne de montage (bâtiment 2), le groupe va directement à la dégustation, à l'entrée principale.

title: Extrait de réunion — notes de frais
script: Before we wrap up today's meeting, I have one more announcement. Starting next month, all travel expense reports must be submitted through the new online system instead of on paper. The system is easy to use, and it'll speed up reimbursements considerably. I know some of you aren't too fond of new software—I wasn't either at first. But it really only takes ten minutes. Jenna from accounting will hold a short training session on Thursday at two. Please write your name on the sign-up sheet by the door if you'd like to attend.

qs.q: What is the main topic of the announcement?
qs.e: Les notes de frais devront être soumises via un nouveau système en ligne.

qs.q: Why does the speaker say, "I wasn't either at first"?
c: To admit she made an error
To show she understands the listeners' concerns
qs.e: Elle reconnaît qu'elle aussi se méfiait du nouveau logiciel : elle comprend les réticences.

qs.q: What are interested listeners asked to do?
c: Write their names on a list
qs.e: « write your name on the sign-up sheet by the door ».

title: Bulletin radio — festival
script: This is Radio Sunrise, and here's an update on this weekend's Riverside Food Festival. Because of the heavy rain expected on Saturday, organizers have decided to move the festival indoors to the Grand Exhibition Hall on Market Street. The festival will still run from eleven a.m. to nine p.m. on both days. More than forty local restaurants will be offering samples, and there'll be cooking demonstrations every hour. Tickets purchased for the outdoor event will be accepted at the door. For updates, follow the festival on social media.

qs.q: What is the broadcast mainly about?
c: A change of venue for an event
qs.e: Le festival est déplacé dans une salle couverte : changement de lieu (venue).

qs.q: Why was the change made?
qs.e: « Because of the heavy rain expected on Saturday ».

qs.q: What does the speaker say about tickets?
c: They are sold only at the door.
Tickets already purchased will be accepted.
qs.e: « Tickets purchased for the outdoor event will be accepted at the door ».

title: Présentation d'une intervenante
script: Good evening, and thank you all for coming to the annual Greenway Business Awards. It's my pleasure to introduce our first speaker, Ms. Valérie Dumont. Ms. Dumont founded Ecopack twelve years ago in her garage. Today, the company employs over three hundred people and supplies recyclable packaging to supermarkets across Europe. Last spring, Ecopack opened its first factory in Canada. Tonight, Ms. Dumont will talk about how small businesses can reduce their environmental impact without increasing costs. Please join me in welcoming her.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the talk?
qs.e: « It's my pleasure to introduce our first speaker ».

qs.q: What does Ecopack produce?
qs.e: « supplies recyclable packaging to supermarkets ».

qs.q: According to the speaker, what happened last spring?
qs.e: « Last spring, Ecopack opened its first factory in Canada ».

title: Message enregistré — support technique
script: Thank you for calling Nexora Technical Support. Our offices are currently closed. Our regular business hours are Monday through Friday, eight a.m. to six p.m. If you're calling about a forgotten password, you can reset it yourself at any time by visiting nexora dot com slash help. For all other issues, please leave a detailed message including your customer number, and a technician will return your call on the next business day. Please note that our offices will also be closed next Monday for a national holiday.

qs.q: Why is the message being played?
qs.e: « Our offices are currently closed ».

qs.q: What can callers do on the Web site?
qs.e: « you can reset it yourself … by visiting nexora.com/help ».

qs.q: What does the speaker say about next Monday?
c: A new service will be launched.
qs.e: « closed next Monday for a national holiday ».

title: Présentation + graphique — ventes
script: Thanks for coming, everyone. As you can see on this chart, our new sports drink had a strong first quarter. Sales in the South were especially impressive, largely because of the television campaign we ran there in February. However, the region with the lowest sales concerns me. We have only two distributors there, so many stores simply don't carry the product. I've asked Hiro to look for additional distributors in that region and report back at our next meeting.

qs.q: What product is being discussed?
qs.e: « our new sports drink ».

qs.q: What contributed to strong sales in one region?
qs.e: « because of the television campaign we ran there in February ».

qs.q: Look at the graphic. Which region will Hiro focus on?
qs.e: Il s'agit de la région aux ventes les plus faibles : l'Ouest (900 unités).

qs.q: The quarterly report must be submitted ------- Friday at 5 P.M.
qs.e: « by » marque une date limite (au plus tard). « until » s'emploie pour une action qui dure jusqu'à un moment (work until 5 P.M.).

qs.q: Ms. Tanaka has worked for Avion Logistics ------- more than ten years.
qs.e: Present perfect + durée → « for ». « since » introduit un point de départ (since 2015).

qs.q: The new accounting software will be installed ------- the weekend to avoid disrupting operations.
qs.e: Devant un groupe nominal (the weekend), il faut une préposition : « during ». « while / when / as » sont des conjonctions suivies d'une proposition.

qs.q: The marketing team presented a highly ------- proposal to the board of directors.
qs.e: Entre l'adverbe « highly » et le nom « proposal », il faut un adjectif : persuasive.

qs.q: Mr. Okafor ------- the Lyon branch since last March.
qs.e: « since + point de départ » impose le present perfect : has managed.

qs.q: If the shipment ------- on time, production will begin on Monday.
qs.e: 1er conditionnel : if + présent simple, puis will + base verbale. Jamais « will » directement après « if » dans ce cas.

qs.q: Please direct all questions about travel reimbursements to Ms. Duval, ------- handles the department's expenses.
qs.e: Antécédent humain + pronom sujet du verbe « handles » → who. « whom » est complément, « which » s'emploie pour les choses.

qs.q: Neither the regional manager ------- her assistant was available for comment.
qs.e: Corrélation fixe : neither … nor (comme either … or, both … and).

qs.q: The conference room ------- for the board meeting yesterday afternoon.
qs.e: La salle ne réserve pas : elle est réservée → passif. « yesterday » impose le prétérit : was reserved.

qs.q: Customers who wish to ------- their subscription must notify us in writing.
qs.e: « wish to » est suivi de la base verbale : cancel.

qs.q: Galvex Corporation offers a competitive salary and generous ------- such as health insurance and paid leave.
qs.e: « benefits » = avantages sociaux (mutuelle, congés payés…). Profits et revenues concernent les résultats de l'entreprise.

qs.q: The budget proposal was approved ------- the objections of two board members.
qs.e: Devant un groupe nominal → la préposition « despite ». « although » doit être suivi d'une proposition (sujet + verbe).

qs.q: Ms. Rossi requested that all receipts ------- to the accounting department by Thursday.
qs.e: Après request / require / recommend / suggest that → subjonctif (base verbale) : be sent. Niveau B2-C1.

qs.q: Sales of the new tablet have risen ------- since its launch in March.
qs.e: Un verbe (have risen) est modifié par un adverbe : steadily.

qs.q: Hardly ------- the meeting begun when the fire alarm went off.
qs.e: « Hardly … when » entraîne une inversion au past perfect : Hardly had the meeting begun… (niveau C1).

qs.q: The technician will ------- the equipment carefully before it is shipped to the client.
qs.e: Après un modal (will), on emploie la base verbale : inspect.

qs.q: The seminar is intended for employees ------- responsibilities include customer service.
qs.e: Idée de possession (leurs responsabilités) → whose + nom.

qs.q: Please complete the attached form and return ------- to the Human Resources department.
qs.e: Le pronom remplace « the attached form » (singulier, complément) → it.

qs.q: The shipment was delayed, ------- the client was offered a ten percent discount.
qs.e: Cause → conséquence : « so ». « because » introduirait la cause, pas la conséquence.

qs.q: Our new headquarters is ------- larger than the previous building.
qs.e: On renforce un comparatif avec much, far ou significantly : much larger. « more larger » est incorrect.

qs.q: The warranty does not ------- damage caused by improper use of the product.
qs.e: Une garantie « covers » (couvre) certains dommages. Les autres verbes ne se combinent pas avec « warranty … damage ».

qs.q: All visitors are required to sign in at the front desk ------- entering the laboratory.
qs.e: « before + V-ing » : avant d'entrer. « among / between » concernent la position.

qs.q: The company plans to ------- its operations into South America next year.
qs.e: Collocation : expand operations into a market (étendre ses activités à). « increase operations into » n'est pas idiomatique.

qs.q: Employees are encouraged ------- public transportation whenever possible.
qs.e: be encouraged + to + base verbale.

qs.q: Mr. Patel suggested ------- the product launch until the marketing materials are ready.
qs.e: suggest + V-ing (ou suggest that + sujet + base verbale). « suggest to do » est une erreur fréquente.

qs.q: The new procedures will be explained in ------- at Thursday's staff meeting.
qs.e: Expression figée : in detail (en détail), au singulier. « in details » est un calque du français.

qs.q: Each of the participants ------- a certificate at the end of the training course.
qs.e: Le sujet est « Each » (singulier) → receives, malgré « participants » au pluriel.

qs.q: The board of directors ------- to announce its decision on the merger next week.
qs.e: « The board » est traité comme un singulier (cf. « its decision ») → expects.

qs.q: We look forward to ------- you at our annual conference in Seoul.
qs.e: Dans « look forward to », « to » est une préposition → V-ing : seeing.

qs.q: The restaurant has received excellent reviews ------- its opening in May.
qs.e: Present perfect + point de départ (its opening) → since.

qs.q: Of the three proposals, Mr. Ortiz's was the ------- expensive.
qs.e: « Of the three » → superlatif : the least expensive. « less » compare seulement deux éléments.

qs.q: The store will remain open ------- 10 P.M. during the holiday season.
qs.e: Action qui dure jusqu'à un moment (remain open) → until.

qs.q: The marketing director asked her team to prepare a ------- analysis of competitors' prices.
qs.e: Entre « a » et le nom « analysis » → adjectif : thorough (approfondi). Piège orthographique avec « through ».

qs.q: Due to unforeseen circumstances, the concert has been ------- until next month.
qs.e: postpone … until = reporter à. « prolonged » signifie allonger la durée.

qs.q: The renovation of the lobby is expected to be completed ------- three weeks.
qs.e: within + durée = dans un délai de.

qs.q: Mr. Dubois prefers to review contracts ------- rather than rely on his assistant.
qs.e: Pronom réfléchi d'insistance : il les relit lui-même (himself).

qs.q: Our customer service representatives are available ------- the clock to answer your questions.
qs.e: Expression figée : around the clock = 24 h sur 24.

qs.q: Last year's financial results were ------- better than analysts had predicted.
qs.e: Un comparatif (better) est modifié par un adverbe : considerably.

qs.q: The safety inspection ------- every six months by an independent agency.
qs.e: L'inspection est réalisée « by an independent agency » → passif au présent (habitude) : is conducted.

qs.q: The hotel's conference facilities can ------- up to 500 guests.
qs.e: accommodate = pouvoir accueillir (une capacité).

qs.q: Please ------- that the office will be closed on Monday for the national holiday.
qs.e: Formule figée des notes de service : Please note that… (veuillez noter que). « notify » exige un complément de personne.

qs.q: By the time the new CEO arrives in June, the restructuring -------.
qs.e: « By the time » + action future → futur antérieur ; la restructuration subit l'action → passif : will have been completed.

qs.q: The proposal was rejected because it was not financially -------.
qs.e: Après « was » (+ adverbe financially), il faut un adjectif attribut : feasible.

qs.q: Visitors may park in the north lot ------- the main lot is full.
qs.e: Condition → if. « despite » et « during » ne peuvent pas introduire une proposition.

qs.q: Ms. Kowalski was promoted ------- her outstanding work on the Asian market project.
qs.e: Devant un groupe nominal → « because of ». « because » seul exige une proposition.

qs.q: The finance department has ------- reviewed the expense reports from the last quarter.
qs.e: already se place entre has et le participe dans une phrase affirmative. « yet » s'emploie surtout en négation/question (has not reviewed yet).

qs.q: The keynote speaker's presentation was so ------- that the audience asked many questions.
qs.e: so + adjectif + that : so informative that…

qs.q: Ms. Nguyen will be responsible ------- training new staff members in the Singapore office.
qs.e: responsible for + V-ing. « responsible of » est un calque fréquent du français.

qs.q: The company's profits increased ------- 15 percent last year.
qs.e: Variation chiffrée : increase / decrease by X percent.

qs.q: ------- the merger is approved, the two companies will combine their research departments.
qs.e: « Once » (une fois que) introduit une proposition et donne un sens logique. « Despite » et « During » sont des prépositions.

title: E-mail interne
passage:
To: All staff
From: Facilities Department
Subject: Parking lot renovation

Please be advised that the north parking lot will be closed from June 3 to June 14 [[1]] resurfacing work. During this period, employees are encouraged to use the public garage on Elm Street. The company will [[2]] the full cost of parking for all staff members. [[3]] We apologize for any inconvenience and appreciate your [[4]] while the work is being completed.

qs.q: Blank 1
qs.e: Devant un groupe nominal (resurfacing work) → « due to ». « because » exigerait « because of ».

qs.q: Blank 2
qs.e: will + base verbale à l'actif : the company will cover the cost.

qs.q: Blank 3
c: The north lot was originally built in 1998.
The cafeteria menu will change next week.
Simply show your employee badge at the garage entrance.
Thank you for attending yesterday's training session.
qs.e: La phrase doit prolonger l'idée précédente (le parking est pris en charge) : elle explique comment en bénéficier. Les autres sont hors sujet.

qs.q: Blank 4
qs.e: Après le possessif « your », il faut un nom : patience. « patients » désigne des malades.

title: Annonce commerciale
passage: Greenfield Office Supplies is pleased to announce the opening of its [[1]] store in downtown Marseille on April 2. To celebrate, all customers will receive a 15 percent discount on purchases made [[2]] the first two weeks. [[3]] In addition, members of our loyalty program [[4]] double points on every order placed in April.

qs.q: Blank 1
qs.e: Entre « its » et le nom « store », il faut un adjectif : newest.

qs.q: Blank 2
qs.e: Devant un groupe nominal de durée → préposition « throughout » (pendant toute la durée de).

qs.q: Blank 3
c: Our headquarters are located in Lyon.
Please return your visitor badge at reception.
The interview will last about thirty minutes.
This offer cannot be combined with other promotions.
qs.e: La phrase précise les conditions de la remise annoncée juste avant ; « In addition » introduit ensuite un second avantage.

qs.q: Blank 4
qs.e: Sujet pluriel (members) + avantage futur (en avril) → will earn. « earns » ne s'accorde pas.

title: Lettre à un candidat
passage:
Dear Mr. Lindqvist,

Thank you for your interest in the position of logistics coordinator at Norvale Shipping. We were [[1]] impressed by your experience in international freight, and we would like to invite you to an interview at our Gothenburg office on Tuesday, May 9, at 10:00 A.M. [[2]] Please bring a copy of your driver's license, as the position [[3]] occasional travel to our regional warehouses. If this time is not convenient, please contact me so that we can [[4]] another date.

Sincerely,
Helena Strand, Human Resources

qs.q: Blank 1
qs.e: Un adjectif/participe (impressed) est modifié par un adverbe : particularly.

qs.q: Blank 2
c: The warehouse closes at noon on Fridays.
The interview will last approximately one hour.
qs.e: La phrase complète naturellement l'invitation à l'entretien (sa durée). Les autres n'ont pas de lien logique avec le paragraphe.

qs.q: Blank 3
qs.e: Vérité générale sur le poste → présent simple : the position requires… Le passif « will be required » ne peut pas avoir de complément d'objet ici.

qs.q: Blank 4
qs.e: Après le modal « can », il faut la base verbale : arrange (organiser, fixer).

title: Note de service
passage:
MEMO
To: All employees
From: Sustainability Committee
Re: New recycling program

Beginning next Monday, the company will introduce a new recycling program on every floor. Separate bins for paper, plastic, and glass [[1]] in each kitchen area. [[2]], cleaning staff will collect the contents twice a week. We ask that you rinse all containers before placing them in the bins. [[3]] Questions about the program should be [[4]] to Mark Elliot in the facilities office.

qs.q: Blank 1
qs.e: Les poubelles ne placent rien : elles sont placées → passif futur : will be placed.

qs.q: Blank 2
qs.e: On ajoute une information complémentaire → In addition. Aucune opposition n'est exprimée.

qs.q: Blank 3
c: The kitchen will be repainted in the fall.
Unwashed items can contaminate an entire batch of recycling.
Please park in the visitor spaces only.
qs.e: La phrase justifie la consigne précédente (rincer les contenants).

qs.q: Blank 4
qs.e: should be + participe passé : should be directed to (doivent être adressées à).

title: Article de presse locale
passage: BRIGHTON (March 3) — Café Lumière, the popular bakery on Kings Road, will open a second location next month. The new café, located near the train station, will be [[1]] larger than the original shop, with seating for up to 80 customers. Owner Claire Morel says the expansion became necessary [[2]] customers often had to wait outside on weekends. [[3]] The new location will also offer a lunch menu, something [[4]] customers have been requesting for years.

qs.q: Blank 1
qs.e: Un comparatif (larger) est modifié par un adverbe : significantly larger.

qs.q: Blank 2
qs.e: La proposition qui suit explique la cause → because. « despite » ne peut pas introduire une proposition.

qs.q: Blank 3
c: The train station was built in 1840.
Bread prices have fallen across the country.
"We simply didn't have enough tables," she explained.
She plans to retire next year.
qs.e: La citation de la propriétaire illustre directement la cause évoquée juste avant (le manque de place).

qs.q: Blank 4
qs.e: Antécédent non humain (something) + pronom complément → that (ou which). « what » ne suit jamais un nom.

title: E-mail au client
passage:
Dear Ms. Alvarez,

Thank you for your recent order from Bellmont Home. Unfortunately, the blue armchair you selected is temporarily out of stock. We expect to receive new [[1]] from our supplier by the end of the month. [[2]] Alternatively, we can ship the same chair in gray immediately at no additional charge. Please let us know which option you prefer by replying to this e-mail. We [[3]] for any inconvenience this may cause and thank you for your [[4]].

Best regards,
Customer Service Team

qs.q: Blank 1
qs.e: inventory = stock, marchandises. Les autres mots se ressemblent mais n'ont pas de sens ici.

qs.q: Blank 2
c: If you are willing to wait, your order will ship on June 2.
Our showroom has recently been renovated.
Gray is our most popular color this year.
We also sell a wide range of outdoor furniture.
qs.e: « Alternatively » suppose qu'une première option vient d'être proposée : attendre le réassort.

qs.q: Blank 3
qs.e: Après le sujet « We », il faut un verbe conjugué : apologize.

qs.q: Blank 4
qs.e: Après le possessif « your » → nom : understanding (compréhension). Formule figée : thank you for your understanding.

Responsibilities: respond to customer inquiries by phone, e-mail, and chat; resolve booking problems; and identify ways to improve our service.

Requirements: at least two years of experience in customer service; excellent written and spoken English. Knowledge of French or Spanish is a plus.

We offer: a competitive salary, two remote-work days per week, and annual travel discounts.

To apply, send your CV and a cover letter to the Human Resources department by 30 June.

qs.q: What is one of the job's responsibilities?
qs.e: « respond to customer inquiries » = répondre aux questions des clients.

qs.q: What is NOT mentioned as a benefit of the job?
qs.e: Questions « NOT » : éliminez tout ce qui est mentionné. Aucune voiture de fonction n'est proposée.

qs.q: What is suggested about knowledge of French?
c: It will be tested during the interview.
It is an advantage but not necessary.
It is needed for remote work.
qs.e: « is a plus » = un atout, sans être obligatoire.

docs.b:
Small Airline Takes Off
By Peter Lang

When regional carrier SkyNorth launched three years ago, few analysts expected it to survive. The airline started with just two aircraft and a single route between Oslo and Bergen. Today, it operates fourteen planes and serves eleven cities across Scandinavia.

According to CEO Ingrid Solberg, the key to SkyNorth's success has been its focus on punctuality. "Business travelers value reliability above everything else," she says. Last year, 94 percent of SkyNorth flights departed on time, the highest rate of any airline in the region.

The company now plans to add routes to Copenhagen and Helsinki next spring. To finance the expansion, SkyNorth will issue new shares, a move that should raise approximately 60 million euros.

qs.q: What is the article mainly about?
qs.e: Le titre et le premier paragraphe décrivent la réussite de SkyNorth.

qs.q: According to Ms. Solberg, what do business travelers care about most?
qs.e: « Business travelers value reliability above everything else ».

qs.q: The word "issue" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
qs.e: issue new shares = émettre / mettre sur le marché de nouvelles actions. Le sens « problème » est un piège.

qs.q: What is indicated about SkyNorth?
c: It started with a single route.
It will merge with another airline.
qs.e: « a single route between Oslo and Bergen ». 94 est un pourcentage de ponctualité, pas un nombre d'avions.

To: Guest Relations, Mariposa Hotel
From: James Whitfield
Date: 2 September
Subject: My recent stay

Dear Guest Relations,

I stayed at the Mariposa Hotel from 28 to 31 August while attending a business conference. Although the staff were very helpful, I was disappointed with my room. I had booked a room with a sea view, but I was given one facing the parking lot. In addition, the air conditioning was noisy at night, which made it difficult to sleep. I asked for a different room on my second day, but none were available.

I have stayed at your hotel several times and have always enjoyed it. I hope this was an exception.

Sincerely,
James Whitfield

To: James Whitfield
From: Lucia Ferrante, Guest Relations Manager
Date: 4 September
Subject: RE: My recent stay

Dear Mr. Whitfield,

Thank you for taking the time to write to us, and please accept our sincere apologies. Because of a booking error, several guests did not receive the rooms they had reserved during the last week of August. As a valued returning guest, you will be refunded the difference between a sea-view room and a standard room. We would also like to offer you a complimentary night on your next visit. The air-conditioning unit in your room has since been replaced.

Kind regards,
Lucia Ferrante

qs.q: Why did Mr. Whitfield stay at the hotel?
c: He was interviewing for a job.
qs.e: « while attending a business conference ».

qs.q: What does Mr. Whitfield say about the hotel staff?
qs.e: « the staff were very helpful ».

qs.q: According to Ms. Ferrante, what caused the problem with the room?
qs.e: « Because of a booking error ».

qs.q: What is suggested about Mr. Whitfield?
c: He has stayed at the Mariposa Hotel before.
qs.e: Il écrit « I have stayed at your hotel several times » et la réponse le qualifie de « returning guest ».

qs.q: What will Mr. Whitfield receive?
qs.e: « a complimentary night on your next visit ». Il ne sera remboursé que de la différence de prix, pas intégralement.
